memory_candidates.content: In ~/.dotfiles/modules/home/email/agent-tools/, email-reindex (defined in mbsync.nix, not agent-tools/) is explicitly commented 'NOT part of the 5-binary agent contract' and does not use mkPreamble/mkMutationPreamble or --account at all -- it's account-agnostic (notmuch new --no-hooks over the whole db). The actual five mkPreamble-sharing binaries are email-census, email-classify, email-unsubscribe-extract, email-archive-confirmed, email-delete-confirmed. Task descriptions referencing 'the five wrapper binaries' should be checked against this list rather than assumed.

When fixing a shared getopts-style arg-parsing loop that multiple downstream consumers inherit, check whether any consumer relies on the loop's catch-all/passthrough behavior (e.g. leftover positional args becoming a query string) before adding a blanket reject/error case -- a per-token-value alias (matching only the specific ambiguous literal values) combined with a loud log() note is often the safer minimal fix versus a uniform hard-reject.

For a Nix home-manager module change that generates a shell script via pkgs.writeShellScriptBin, you can verify both the Nix evaluation AND the generated bash's runtime behavior without ever running home-manager switch: build a standalone derivation via 'nix build -f <scratch.nix>' where the scratch expression does 'builtins.getFlake "<absolute-repo-path>"' to get the real flake's homeConfigurations.<user>.pkgs, then call the target pkgs.writeShellScriptBin with the module's helper function directly. This produces a real /nix/store binary built through the live flake's pkgs that can be run directly (with env vars overridden to avoid touching real state) to functionally verify arg-parsing logic pre-deployment.
